run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Social Network
Namespace: social-network

A social network with unidirectional follow relationships, implemented with loosely-coupled microservices, communicating with each other via Thrift RPCs.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The only anomaly with its own failure evidence in this Run is the Jaeger observability Deployment in namespace social-network: it was rolled out to 2 replicas whose pod template requires pod anti-affinity across hostnames and mounts the single ReadWriteOnce openebs-hostpath claim jaeger-pvc, and its second pod (jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-gwcj9) is Pending/Unschedulable. The Deployment reports 1/2 available replicas and condition Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable), and the alerting rules PendingPodsDetected and PodSchedulingFailure are firing for that pod. The scheduling failure message names both constraints: it cannot go on sregym-worker3 because of the required anti-affinity rule, and the other nodes conflict with the volume's node affinity (the PV is bound to sregym-worker3, the node where the surviving replica runs). Facts: Deployment jaeger was scaled 0->1 under ReplicaSet jaeger-7d8548779 at 16:58:38 and then rolled to new ReplicaSet jaeger-9fd7cdb7c 'from 0 to 2' at 16:58:48; the old pod was stopped at 16:58:48. For the Social Network application itself I found no failing operation in the sampled window: all 142 spans returned for nginx-web-server between 16:58:30 and 16:59:05 carry http.status_code=200 (2 /wrk2-api/post/compose, 12 /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read, 22 /wrk2-api/home-timeline/read), all 26 application Services have ready endpoints, there are 0 networkpolicies in the namespace, and all 28 pods in social-network other than the pending jaeger pod are Running/Ready with 0 restarts. Four services logged mongodb connection/index errors at 16:58:40-16:58:44 while their mongodb pods were still starting; those look transient since later mongo client spans succeeded, and no alert names them. Note the window is effectively only ~27 s of application runtime (last line at 16:59:02), so this is a sampled view, not a whole-incident view.

claims.text: Deployment jaeger in namespace social-network declares spec.replicas=2, a requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution podAntiAffinity on topologyKey kubernetes.io/hostname for pods labelled service=jaeger, and mounts persistentVolumeClaim jaeger-pvc at /jaeger-data (image docker.io/jaegertracing/all-in-one:1.57).

Deployment jaeger status (read 2026-11-21T17:01:47Z) shows replicas=2, availableReplicas=1, readyReplicas=1, unavailableReplicas=1, and condition Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable ('Deployment does not have minimum availability').

Pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-gwcj9 in namespace social-network is Pending with condition PodScheduled=False, reason Unschedulable, message '0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 2 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict. preemption: 0/4 nodes are available...'; it has no assigned node and no pod IP, while its sibling jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-gsrw9 is Running/Ready on sregym-worker3 (pod IP 10.244.125.56).

Two Warning FailedScheduling events name pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-gwcj9: at 16:58:49 '0/4 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match pod anti-affinity rules, 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 2 node(s) didn't find available persistent volumes to bind', and at 16:58:51 the same with '2 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict'.

PersistentVolumeClaim jaeger-pvc (namespace social-network) has accessModes [ReadWriteOnce], storageClassName openebs-hostpath and is Bound to volume pvc-2367e879-b3f5-4348-ab88-c20359edfd18; that PersistentVolume has required nodeAffinity kubernetes.io/hostname In [sregym-worker3] and accessModes [ReadWriteOnce].

The jaeger Deployment was changed during the window: events show 'Scaled up replica set jaeger-7d8548779 from 0 to 1' at 16:58:38, then 'Stopping container jaeger' for pod jaeger-7d8548779-frhbr and 'Scaled up replica set jaeger-9fd7cdb7c from 0 to 2' at 16:58:48; ReplicaSet jaeger-9fd7cdb7c (owner Deployment jaeger, created 2026-11-21T16:58:48Z) has spec.replicas=2 and status availableReplicas=1, readyReplicas=1, replicas=2.

The only alerting rules in state firing at query time are PendingPodsDetected and PodSchedulingFailure, both for pod jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-gwcj9 in namespace social-network (activeAt 2026-11-21T17:00:09Z, value 1); the other loaded rules (including ServiceEndpointDown, DeploymentNotReady, HighRequestErrorRate, HighRequestLatency, KubePodNotReady) are inactive. This is the rules' state at the moment of the query, which can be after the authorized window.

In the sampled traces for nginx-web-server between 16:58:30 and 16:59:05, no error span appears: 142 spans are shown with 0 error rows, and every HTTP span is http.status_code=200 (/wrk2-api/home-timeline/read 22 spans, /wrk2-api/user-timeline/read 12 spans, /wrk2-api/post/compose 2 spans); downstream server spans (compose-post-service, user-timeline-service, home-timeline-service, social-graph-service, post-storage-service, text-service, url-shorten-service, user-mention-service, unique-id-service, media-service, user-service) are all status not_recorded with no error details. This is a biased sample, not a failure rate.

All pods in namespace social-network other than jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-gwcj9 were Running with ready=true and restartCount=0 at 16:59:08 (28 pods returned; only jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-gwcj9 shows phase Pending with no container statuses).

The 26 application ClusterIP Services in social-network all resolve to ready endpoints (e.g. compose-post-service 10.244.234.130:9090, nginx-thrift 10.244.234.134:8080, user-timeline-service 10.244.234.133:9090, social-graph-service 10.244.125.57:9090), and the namespace contains 0 networkpolicies, so no selector mismatch or network isolation is observed on the request path.

Four services logged mongodb connect/index failures only in their first seconds: post-storage-service at 16:58:40/16:58:41/16:58:43, user-service at 16:58:41/16:58:42/16:58:44, url-shorten-service at 16:58:43 and user-timeline-service at 16:58:41, each 'Error in createIndexes: No suitable servers found: `serverSelectionTimeoutMS` expired: [unknown connection error calling ismaster on '<svc>-mongodb:27017']' plus 'Failed to create mongodb index, try again'.

The same services' mongodb calls succeeded later in the window: spans post_storage_mongo_insert_client (614us), social_graph_mongo_find_client (783us), url_mongo_insert_client (602us) and user_timeline_mongo_find_client (9-18us) were recorded with no error status, and one full /wrk2-api/post/compose trace completed with http.status_code=200 across compose-post-service, text-service, user-mention-service, url-shorten-service, post-storage-service, user-timeline-service, social-graph-service, home-timeline-service, media-service and user-service.

The blackbox tcp_connect probes recorded probe_success=0 at 16:59:00 for 11 of 13 social-network targets (compose-post-service, media-frontend, media-service, nginx-thrift, post-storage-service, social-graph-service, text-service, unique-id-service, url-shorten-service, user-service, user-timeline-service) and 1 for home-timeline-service and user-mention-service; these pods were created between 16:58:38 and 16:58:53.

All 13 blackbox-social-network scrape targets currently report health 'up' with no lastError and lastScrape after 16:59:00 (e.g. compose-post-service.social-network:9090 lastScrape 2026-11-21T16:59:01Z, nginx-thrift.social-network:8080 16:59:39Z), and the wrk2 load generator's returned lines show one completed 10 s round at 16:58:58 with '1024 requests in 10.00s' and 'Requests/sec: 102.38' and no non-2xx line among the returned lines.

Loki holds no social-network log lines before 16:58:40: a per-app count_over_time covering 14:00-16:58:40 has its first value at 16:58:40, and the error-pattern count over the same window also starts at 16:58:40; the earliest application line returned was compose-post-service starting at 16:58:39.196.

The metrics-discovery queries for application-level series returned nothing: get_metric_names for {__name__=~"rpc_.*|http_.*|traces_.*|app_.*"} returned no names, and get_label_values for service_name on traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned no values, while the names present for namespace social-network are cAdvisor/container_*, probe_* and scrape_*/up. The otel-spanmetrics scrape targets themselves report up=1 at 16:59:05 (otel-collector.observe:8889 and :8890).

Monitoring-stack startup warnings were recorded in namespace observe between 16:56:45 and 16:58:22 (loki-0 readiness probe 503 at 16:58:08, StatefulSet loki FailedUpdate at 16:57:29, FailedMount 'timed out waiting for the condition' on promtail/loki-gateway/kube-state-metrics/pushgateway); no alert names any observe object.

The second Jaeger replica can never schedule because the Deployment jaeger combines a required host-level pod anti-affinity with one ReadWriteOnce openebs-hostpath claim bound to node sregym-worker3: the surviving replica occupies sregym-worker3, so anti-affinity excludes it, and every other node is rejected by the volume's node affinity ('2 node(s) had volume node affinity conflict').

The probe_success=0 readings at 16:59:00 are first-scrape artifacts of the 16:58:38-16:58:53 pod start rather than an application outage, because the same targets report health 'up' with later lastScrape times and the sampled traces in the same seconds returned HTTP 200; the probes are tcp_connect, so they test listening ports only.

The mongodb createIndexes/connection errors at 16:58:40-16:58:44 are not the cause of the fired alerts: no alert names those services or mongodb pods, they occurred once per service during startup ('try again'), and later mongo client spans in the same window succeeded, so they read as startup ordering rather than a persisting dependency failure.

A Service selector mismatch or network policy blocking traffic is rejected as the cause of the jaeger pod's state: the unschedulable reason is PodScheduled=False from anti-affinity plus volume node affinity, all 26 application Services have ready endpoint addresses, and namespace social-network has 0 networkpolicies.

Fix the jaeger Deployment scheduling conflict: either run it with 1 replica, or drop the requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution host anti-affinity, or provision storage that allows the second replica on another node (ReadWriteMany or no node-bound local PV), or remove the jaeger-pvc mount if the all-in-one image keeps traces in memory.

Restore application RED metrics: the HighRequestErrorRate and HighRequestLatency rules depend on traces_span_metrics_calls_total / traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket, which discovery queries did not find, so application error and latency alerts are currently blind; verify the otel-collector spanmetrics exporter -> Prometheus scrape path.

gaps: Application-level metrics are missing from this Prometheus: get_metric_names for {__name__=~"rpc_.*|http_.*|traces_.*|app_.*"} and get_label_values for service_name on traces_span_metrics_calls_total both returned nothing, so error-rate and latency of the social-network services could not be measured; those queries returned no series and that is not evidence of zero errors.

Only about 27 seconds of application runtime fall inside the authorized window (all social-network pods were created 16:58:38-16:58:53 and the latest in-window span is at 16:59:02); earlier history is unavailable (no Loki lines before 16:58:40, Jaeger in-memory store reset when the jaeger pod was recreated at 16:58:52), so behaviour before and after the window is unknown.

The change_history integration is not available, so who or what applied the jaeger Deployment change at 16:58:48 and which exact pod-template field changed cannot be verified; the old ReplicaSet jaeger-7d8548779 was already deleted, so its template cannot be compared with jaeger-9fd7cdb7c.

Whether the unschedulable second Jaeger replica has any consumer-visible consequence is not established: the application reports spans to otel-collector.observe.svc.cluster.local:6831 and Jaeger returned traces during the window, so no user-facing effect of the missing replica was observed, and impact beyond the Deployment/Pod is unverified.

Services jaeger, jaeger-agent, jaeger-collector and jaeger-query in social-network define label selectors but no ports and have no Endpoints objects in the returned list; whether anything depends on them could not be determined, and Jaeger query access worked through jaeger-9fd7cdb7c-gsrw9.
Recovery of the 11 targets that read probe_success=0 at 16:59:00 cannot be evaluated inside the authorized window; their targets report health 'up' only at the post-window observation time.
next_steps: Review the jaeger Deployment manifest together with the cluster's storage classes (openebs-hostpath is node-bound RWO) and choose one scheduling model: 1 replica, RWX/multi-node storage, or no required host anti-affinity.

Confirm whether the second Jaeger replica is required by any consumer (jaeger-query/jaeger-collector consumers) and correct the port-less jaeger/jaeger-agent/jaeger-collector/jaeger-query Services if they are meant to be used.

Repair or validate the OpenTelemetry span-metrics export so traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket reach Prometheus, then re-check HighRequestErrorRate and HighRequestLatency.
Once the load generator runs again, re-sample nginx-web-server traces and application logs over a longer window to confirm no request-path degradation accompanies the jaeger replica shortage.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.

view.span_groups_note: span_groups summarizes the spans shown in content; spans the adapter sampled out are not counted in any group.

notes: The tool limited the query to the window 2026-11-21T16:55:00Z to 2026-11-21T16:59:05Z; this filter cannot be turned off.

The longest range reads 120 s back, so evaluation started at 2026-11-21T16:57:00Z: the requested window start plus 120 s, rounded up to the step, at most one step later. No point counts a line from before 2026-11-21T16:55:00Z.
view.cannot_prove: A line that is not returned is unknown, not proof that nothing was logged: only limit lines are shown (the newest), and retention, ingest delay, the label selector and line filters can leave gaps. The timestamp is when the line was ingested or parsed, not necessarily when the event happened. A metric query counts only lines inside the query window.
